name: Farina Blanc-Mange
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: corn-starch, wet in a little cold water
ingredients.originalText: 4 tablespoonfuls corn-starch, wet in a little cold water

ingredients.name: eggs, well beaten—whites and yolks separately
ingredients.originalText: 3 eggs, well beaten—whites and yolks separately

instructions.text: Heat the milk to boiling; stir in the corn-starch and salt, and boil together fifteen minutes (in a farina-kettle) before the eggs are added.
Add the yolks, beaten light, with the sugar; boil two minutes longer, stirring all the while; remove the mixture from the fire, and beat in the whipped whites while it is boiling hot.
Pour into a mould wet with cold water, and set in a cold place.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Heat the milk to boiling; stir in the corn-starch and salt, and boil together fifteen minutes (in a farina-kettle) before the eggs are added.
2. Add the yolks, beaten light, with the sugar; boil two minutes longer, stirring all the while; remove the mixture from the fire, and beat in the whipped whites while it is boiling hot.
3. Pour into a mould wet with cold water, and set in a cold place.
4. Eat with sugar and cream.
